paul.name: Paul
paul.role: Writer who sent Timothy and longs to see the Thessalonians
paul.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
paul.importance: Paul recalls how he and his team worked among the Thessalonians. He says Satan hindered his visits. He sent Timothy to learn about their faith. Timothy’s good news comforts Paul. Paul asks that the letter be read to all the brothers.
paul.connections: He writes with Silvanus and Timothy. He sent Timothy to the Thessalonians.

silas.name: Silvanus
silas.role: Co-sender named with Paul and Timothy
silas.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
silas.importance: The letter names Silvanus in the opening line with Paul and Timothy. The letter says “we” after that. It says nothing else about him by name.
silas.connections: The letter names him second, between Paul and Timothy.

timothy.name: Timothy
timothy.role: Co-sender whom Paul sent to the Thessalonians
timothy.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
timothy.importance: Paul sends Timothy to establish and comfort the Thessalonians in their faith. Timothy comes back with glad news of their faith and love. The news comforts Paul in his distress and affliction.
timothy.connections: He is named with Paul and Silvanus. Paul calls him our brother and God’s servant.

jesus.name: Jesus Christ
jesus.role: Lord who rose from the dead and will come
jesus.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
jesus.importance: Paul says the Thessalonians wait for God’s Son from heaven. Paul says Jesus died and rose again. He says the dead in Christ will rise first. He tells the readers to comfort one another with these words.
jesus.connections: Paul calls him the Lord Jesus Christ and God’s Son. He says God raised him from the dead.

word.languageNote: This is the dictionary form of the name “Jesus.”
